overview: The West Medford Community Center held its 2026 Martin Luther King Jr. Day celebration, centering on the theme "If We Don't Quit" through a program of historical reflections, award presentations, and a keynote address. The body honored local leaders and explored the intersection of civic legacy and contemporary efforts to address systemic inequality.

items.title: Opening Reflections: Legacies of Cobb and Lewis
items.summary: Speakers presented biographical tributes to cancer researcher Dr. Jewel Plummer Cobb and civil rights leader John Lewis to establish the morning's historical context.

items.title: Poetry Reading: "If We Don't Quit"
items.summary: Terry Carter performed an original poem that cataloged the necessary actions for social progress and the validation of past leaders' sacrifices.

items.title: Presentation of the Third Annual Drum Major Awards
items.summary: The center presented awards for civic engagement, arts, and faith to Clarence Ed Ligon (posthumously), Adele Travisano, and Stacey Clayton.

items.title: Drum Major Awards: Legacy Presentation
items.summary: Gwendolyn Lee was honored with the Legacy Award for her century of influence in West Medford, with Rachel Tanner accepting on her behalf.

items.title: Musical Performance: "If I Can Help Somebody"
items.summary: Athene Wilson performed a vocal selection following an acknowledgment of the West Medford Community Center's 90th anniversary.

items.title: Community Building Word Search
items.summary: Attendees participated in a collaborative table exercise using a civil rights-themed word search to encourage social engagement and shared learning.

items.title: Poetry Reading: Max Heinegg
items.summary: Medford Poet Laureate Max Heinegg recited Langston Hughes' "Mother to Son" and an original piece of advice for students facing current societal challenges.

items.title: Keynote Address: Harvard’s Legacy of Slavery Initiative
items.summary: Dr. Sarah Naomi Bleich discussed Harvard University's historical ties to slavery and current reparative efforts, emphasizing the importance of institutional accountability and persistence in public health.

items.title: Communal Song and The Charge
items.summary: The assembly sang "We Shall Overcome" before Jill Harvey delivered a charge to the community to choose communal love and self-awareness over chaos.

items.title: Acknowledgments and Adjournment
items.summary: Executive Director Lisa Crossman thanked the event's organizers, volunteers, and sponsors, including Tufts University and the Mystic Valley branch of the NAACP.

subject: Martin Luther King Jr. Day Celebration
